'''Lane P. Hughston''' (born 24 December 1951) is an American [[mathematician]].

== Early life and education ==
Lane P. Hughston was born in Corpus Christi, Texas, and raised in Dallas, Texas, where he attended J. J. Pershing Elementary School, Benjamin Franklin Junior High School, and [[Hillcrest High School (Dallas)|Hillcrest High School]]. He is the son of Edward Wallace Hughston and Joan Palmer Hughston.<ref>T. L. Hulsey (2020) ''25 Texas Heroes''. Stagirite Press, Ft Worth, Texas. {{ISBN|1-883853-06-0}}</ref>

In 1969 he took first place in the nationwide [[Regeneron Science Talent Search | Westinghouse Science Talent Search]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Science Talent Search 1969 |url=https://www.societyforscience.org/regeneron-sts/science-talent-search-1969/ |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=Society for Science |language=en-US}}</ref>
He holds an MA and a DPhil from the [[University of Oxford]], where he was a [[Rhodes Scholar]]  based at [[Magdalen College, Oxford| Magdalen College]].<ref> {{Cite web |title=Rhodes Scholar Database |url=https://www.rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk/scholar-community/rhodes-scholar-database/ |access-date=2025-10-25 |website=Rhodes Trust |language=en-UK}} </ref> His doctoral studies in mathematics were carried out under the supervision of  [[Roger Penrose]].<ref>[https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=14163 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref> 

==Career==
After completing his doctorate he held a Junior Research Fellowship at [[Wolfson College, Oxford]] and then was Darby Fellow and Tutor in Applied Mathematics at [[Lincoln College, Oxford]].<ref>Oxford University Gazette, No. 3810 Volume CX, Thursday, 29 May 1980, p. 695. </ref>

Later, Hughston worked as a financial engineer at [[Robert Fleming & Co.|Robert Fleming & Co. Limited]], London, and at [[Merrill Lynch]], London, and then as Professor of Mathematics at [[King's College London]], [[Imperial College London]], [[Brunel University London]] and, more recently, [[Goldsmiths, University of London]].<ref> {{Cite web |title=Lane Palmer Hughston |url=https://www.gold.ac.uk/computing/people/hughston-lane/ |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=Goldsmiths, University of London |language=en}}</ref>

He has held visiting appointments at the [[University of Texas at Austin]], [[King's College London]], the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]], and [[University College London]].{{Citation needed|date=August 2025}}
He has carried out research in [[general relativity]], [[cosmology]], [[twistor theory]], [[quantum mechanics]], [[quantum information]], [[statistical mechanics]], [[mathematical finance]]  and [[music theory]].<ref> {{Cite web |title=Lane P. Hughston |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=ASy_EF4AAAAJ&view_op=list_works |access-date=2025-10-25 |website=Google Scholar |language=en}}</ref> Hughston served for sixteen years as Editor-in-Chief at [[International Journal of Theoretical and Applied Finance]] over the period 2007 to 2022,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Grasselli | first1=Matheus R. | title=Editorial | journal=International Journal of Theoretical and Applied Finance | date=2023 | volume=26 | article-number=2301001 | doi=10.1142/S021902492301001X | url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/10.1142/S021902492301001X | url-access=subscription }}</ref> the final year being as co-Editor-in-Chief alongside M. R. Grasselli. In 2008, in collaboration with [[Mark H. A. Davis]], he organized the Fifth World Congress of the Bachelier Finance Society.<ref> {{Cite web |title=Bachelier Finance Society – World Congress |url=https://www.bacheliercongress.com/2008/organization.htm|access-date=2025-10-25 |website=Bachelier Finance Society |language=en}}</ref>
